# Synapse 2.0.20

A step on a model its provider has retired is warned and still runs; Synapse AI's built-in docs point self-hosters at gpt-oss:20b; prices and a Groq model's context window are read from the providers' own pages; and stopping Synapse in a terminal says so once.

## Fixed

- **A step on a retired model is warned, and still runs.** Three models are retired by their providers: Google's `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview` (since May 25, 2026; use `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`), and DeepSeek's `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` (since July 24, 2026). None of them is offered in a model picker any more. A saved step on one of them still runs, because a provider can go on answering a retired model for a while, and the step shows a warning with the provider's own words and the date, so you can choose another model in time. If the provider then refuses the call, Synapse answers it from another model of the same provider where one fits, as it already does for any model that is gone.
- **A model is set aside only when its own refusal names it.** When a provider says a model is gone, Synapse stops offering that model for your workspace. It used to do so whichever model the error named, so another call's refusal could set aside a model that still worked. Now only the model the error names is set aside.
- **Prices and a context window from the providers' own pages.** Three prices were out of date: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite ($0.25 in, $1.50 out per 1M tokens) and Together's Kimi K3 ($3.00 in, $15.00 out) cost more than Synapse counted, and Mistral Large 4 less ($0.70 in, $2.10 out). A run's cost estimate, and a spending cap, now read the providers' current prices. Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is also priced by its live name. Separately, Groq serves Qwen 3.8 27B with a 131,072-token context window, much less than the model's own, and Synapse now plans a step's context to what Groq takes.
- **Synapse AI's built-in docs point self-hosters at gpt-oss:20b.** The docs Synapse AI reads to answer questions about the product told self-hosters to `ollama pull mistral`, a model too small for Synapse AI. They now say `ollama pull gpt-oss:20b`, which reads 128K, in step with the docs site.
- **Stopping Synapse in a terminal says so once.** Pressing Ctrl+C on `synapse start` could print "Stopping Synapse..." several times while it shut down. It now says it once, then "Synapse stopped."

PyPI and npm now describe Synapse as "Synapse by SynapseOrch: AI workflows that follow the plan you approved. Self-hosted, any model."

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.20`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
